target.title: fix(models): preserve static provider catalog metadata
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes static provider catalog conversion so resolved runtime models preserve schema-valid provider/model metadata.

## Problem

Static catalog providers can define provider-level request `params`, while individual model rows can define model-level `params`, `compat`, and `mediaInput`. The static catalog conversion path was not preserving that metadata consistently, so downstream model resolution and OpenAI-compatible payload construction could lose information that other configured-provider paths already keep.

The concrete gap fixed here is provider/model metadata propagation in `modelFromProviderStaticCatalog`.

## Changes

- Merge provider-level and model-level `params` when building a runtime model from the static catalog.
- Let model-level `params` override provider-level defaults.
- Preserve model `compat` metadata on the resolved runtime model.
- Preserve model `mediaInput` metadata on the resolved runtime model.
- Add regression coverage for static catalog metadata preservation, tool-capability checks, and OpenAI-compatible payload construction.

## Real behavior proof

Exact command run after this patch:

```text
node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/proof-static-catalog-metadata.test.ts --config test/vitest/vitest.agents.config.ts --reporter verbose
```

Observed proof output, redacted to the relevant runtime/request fields:

```text
STATIC_PROVIDER_CATALOG_METADATA_PROOF {
  "provider": "proof-provider",
  "id": "proof-model",
  "api": "openai-completions",
  "baseUrl": "https://redacted.example/v1",
  "params": {
    "max_completion_tokens": 64000,
    "providerDefault": true,
    "modelDefault": true
  },
  "compat": {
    "supportsTools": true,
    "maxTokensField": "max_completion_tokens"
  },
  "mediaInput": {
    "image": {
      "maxSidePx": 3072,
      "tokenMode": "provider"
    }
  },
  "transport": {
    "headers": {
      "X-Static-Catalog": "redacted"
    }
  },
  "request": {
    "model": "proof-model",
    "max_completion_tokens": 64000,
    "tools": "absent"
  }
}

Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       1 passed (1)
```

What this proves:

- Provider-level `params.max_completion_tokens=32000` and model-level `params.max_completion_tokens=64000` were merged by the static provider catalog resolver, with the model-level value winning.
- The resolved runtime model preserved provider/model params, `compat`, `mediaInput`, and request transport headers.
- `buildOpenAICompletionsParams(...)` consumed the resolved runtime model and emitted `max_completion_tokens: 64000`, proving the metadata reached the request payload path.
- The proof does not depend on live tool execution and does not use the separate `Tool exec not found` session issue as evidence.

## Additional validation

Focused local checks were run for the touched files:

```text

node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/model.static-catalog.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/model.static-catalog.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/model.test.ts src/agents/openai-transport-stream.test.ts

```

```text

```

## Scope note

This PR is limited to static provider catalog metadata propagation. It does not add a new config key, change session/tool policy, or depend on the separate live-session `Tool exec not found` investigation.

target.title: refactor(voice): dedupe talk audio primitives into OpenClawKit
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Follow-up cleanup to #102901 (universal talk waveform, issue #102895). That feature exposed how much duplicated audio plumbing the talk stack carries: two near-identical buffered TTS clip players (iOS `TalkBufferedAudioPlayer` and macOS `TalkAudioPlayer`, each with its own continuation box, watchdog, and now level meter), a macOS `TalkPlaybackResult` struct that field-for-field duplicated ElevenLabsKit's `StreamingPlaybackResult`, five separate `AVAudioPCMBuffer` RMS implementations, two identical metered-PCM stream passthrough wrappers, and two copies of the ElevenLabs PCM-then-mp3-retry block inside `TalkModeManager`.

## Why This Change Was Made

One canonical implementation per concept, at the owning boundary:

- **`TalkBufferedAudioPlayer` moves to OpenClawKit** (gated `Talk && canImport(ElevenLabsKit)` like the shim, so watch builds compile it out) and serves both apps; macOS `TalkAudioPlayer` + `TalkPlaybackResult` are deleted. The iOS `TalkBufferedAudioPlaying` test seam stays and the shared class conforms.
- **`TalkAudioLevel.rms(buffer:)`** replaces the five per-file buffer-RMS copies (iOS relay tap, iOS `AudioTapDiagnostics`, macOS `TalkModeRuntime`, `VoiceWakeRuntime`, `MicLevelMonitor`).
- **`PCMPlaybackEnvelope.metering(_:sampleRate:)`** absorbs the identical passthrough wrappers from iOS `TalkModeManager` and macOS `TalkModeController`.
- **`playElevenLabsStream`** collapses `TalkModeManager`'s duplicated PCM playback + failure-classification + mp3-retry blocks into one helper.

No behavior change intended; net **−378 lines**.

## User Impact

None visible. Same playback, metering, and fallback behavior on every route; less drift risk the next time any of it changes.

## Evidence

- `apps/shared/OpenClawKit`: `swift build` + `swift test` — waveform math, audio level (incl. new buffer-RMS test), and voice-note recorder suites pass (23 tests).
- `apps/macos`: `swift build` clean; focused suites incl. the migrated `TalkBufferedAudioPlayerTests` pass (36 + 2 tests).
- iOS: xcodegen + `xcodebuild` (OpenClaw scheme incl. watch target) — BUILD SUCCEEDED; the new shared player compiles out of the watch variant via the `canImport` gate, matching `ElevenLabsKitShim`.
- Structured review: autoreview (codex, gpt-5.5) on the branch diff — clean, zero accepted findings.

target.title: fix: keep heredoc bodies out of shell stage splits
target.body:
Closes #102875

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators reading channel tool-status footers could see heredoc body text rendered as phantom shell commands when an exec command writes multiline content with `<<EOF` and then runs a later command that fails.

In the reported Telegram footer, email body lines such as `sc-carwhi(100)` and `Gracias.` were shown as command stages, which made a normal self-correcting turn look like the agent had hallucinated broken commands.

## Why This Change Was Made

The top-level shell scanner already respected quotes and escapes, but it still visited separator characters inside heredoc bodies. This change teaches the scanner to recognize `<<` / `<<-` heredoc markers, parse quoted or escaped terminators, and skip the body until the matching terminator line before continuing normal stage and pipe splitting.

This keeps the change bounded to display-summary parsing; it does not try to validate full shell syntax or change command execution.

## User Impact

Users and operators now get clearer exec status footers for scripts that write multiline files or inline content before running follow-up commands. Heredoc body text is no longer mislabeled as failed commands, while real commands after the heredoc terminator are still summarized.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tool-display.test.ts --reporter=verbose` — passed, 47 tests.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/agents/tool-display-exec-shell.ts src/agents/tool-display.test.ts` — passed.

target.body: Fixes #103013. AI-assisted: Codex was used for implementation, testing, and simulator validation. ## What Problem This Solves Fixes an issue where users opening iOS Settings -> Privacy saw a redundant standalone Privacy status card alongside separate Location controls containing overlapping information. The Location UI also mixed OpenClaw's sharing preference with the actual iOS authorization level, displayed unnecessary guidance after permission denial, and could make the Notifications section difficult to reach. ## Why This Change Was Made This makes the Location card the single source of truth for location sharing: - removes the redundant standalone Privacy status card - places the Location Sharing toggle directly on the Location row - presents Access Level as a read-only value - uses Apple's `While Using the App` and `Always` terminology - derives Access Level from the actual iOS authorization, including when OpenClaw sharing is off - hides Access Level and redundant guidance when permission is denied - opens the app-specific iOS Settings page when a user retries after denial - refreshes authorization state whenever the app returns to the active scene - keeps toggle-off as OpenClaw sharing intent without pretending to downgrade the OS permission - improves VoiceOver output, Dynamic Type wrapping, and loading-state layout stability - restores reliable scrolling to the top of the Privacy screen ## User Impact Users now see one clear Location section that distinguishes OpenClaw's sharing state from the permission retained by iOS. target.title: Interactive parity with the Codex runtime: ask-user-question · plan mode · goal mode
target.body:
> **The agent that asks, plans, and pursues.** This PR gives every OpenClaw session the three interactive primitives Codex-native users already have: the agent can ask structured questions (options + "(Recommended)" + free-text "Other", answerable from any surface), enter a real plan mode (read-only enforcement, a live plan panel, approve-to-execute), and pursue a long-running goal unattended behind a safety-gated continuation driver with a visible "Pursuing goal" chip.

Master hub: #102260 (architecture diagrams, the full test map, and the follow-up roadmap live there).

![Interactive parity demo: mode selector → plan mode with a live checklist in the right sidebar → inline approval → agent question answered inline](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/100yenadmin/openclaw/c57fe74c64e15e1de7a76e742598904ff207c849/docs/assets/interactive-parity/parity-demo.gif)

*The full flow — plan mode, the live plan pane, inline approval, and an inline agent question. A [30s narrated walkthrough](https://github.com/100yenadmin/openclaw/releases/download/interactive-parity-media-v1/parity-demo.mp4) covers goal mode too.*

## Why this shape
The primitives were **already merged** (`update_plan` experimental, goal state tools, a codex user-input bridge, `stream:plan` events, exec-approval UI, Telegram/Slack buttons) — this PR is the completion layer, and every feature rides an existing choke point rather than inventing a parallel system. One branch, **take-apart commit groups** (reviewable and revertable independently; happy to split into stacked PRs on request) — the three feature groups, then a Control-UI pass bringing the surface to Codex-Desktop parity (inline composer cards, right-sidebar plan, mode selector, goal modal):

| Commits | Group | Delivers |
|---|---|---|
| 1–11 | **Question infra** | `ask_user_question` tool · global QuestionManager (exec-approval pattern) · `question.list/resolve` + events · Control-UI card · Telegram/Slack buttons + proactive push · `/answer` · restart expiry-sweep · codex-bridge convergence (structured vs free-text race) |
| 12–21 | **Plan mode** | plan-state slot + `enter/exit_plan_mode` · read-only gate at the single before-tool-call choke point · `update_plan` promoted default-on · live plan panel · `/plan` commands + structured channel summaries · exit-plan approval rides the question infra |
| 22–27 | **Goal mode** | continuation driver (debounced, 4-gated, never self-re-arms) · durable no-progress ceiling · `/goal set/edit/pause/resume/stop --budget` · "Pursuing goal" pill + edit modal · single-source `goal.updated` · behind `tools.experimental.goalDriver` |
| 28–36 | **Control-UI parity pass** | composer goal-pill Lit-race fix · questions & plan-approval as **inline composer cards** (modals retired) · active plan **docked in the right sidebar** · **mode selector** (off/plan/goal, mutually exclusive) by the gear · goal-editor **modal** with card chrome · whole-program type + lint clean |

## What each feature does

### 1 · Structured questions
`ask_user_question` (1-3 questions, 2-4 options, first recommended, auto-"Other") parks the *tool* on a global-manager promise — the exec-approval pattern — so the answer can come from anywhere: an **inline card in the chat composer** (Codex-Desktop style, not a page-locking modal), Telegram inline buttons or Slack Block Kit (pushed proactively to the turn-source chat, deduped), or `/answer <n|text>` on any channel. Ask on Telegram, answer in the browser. No default timeout (humans sleep); a gateway restart expires pending questions loudly (`question.expired`) instead of hanging. Codex-runtime sessions converge: their `request_user_input` (already held open as a JSON-RPC request) now renders the same card, racing the structured answer against the legacy next-free-text path.

![The agent's question rendered inline in the composer: numbered options, a Recommended chip, an "Other" free-text option, with 1-of-N paging](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/100yenadmin/openclaw/c57fe74c64e15e1de7a76e742598904ff207c849/docs/assets/interactive-parity/question-inline.png)

### 2 · Plan mode
The **mode selector by the gear** (or `/plan` / `enter_plan_mode`) puts the session in a read-only collaboration mode enforced as a **core policy at the one choke point every tool execution funnels through** — built-ins incl. exec and subagent spawn, plugin/MCP-backed, catalog, code-mode, client tools. The agent researches and maintains a live checklist (`update_plan`, promoted from experimental with a kill-switch) that ticks in real time in the **right-sidebar plan pane** (always viewable, full rendered plan; a compact chip stays inline); `exit_plan_mode` persists the plan to `~/.openclaw/agents/<id>/plans/` and asks for approval as an **inline composer card** (one pipeline for all human-in-the-loop moments); reject-with-feedback loops the agent back into planning. The mode selector keeps plan and goal mutually exclusive.

![Plan mode: the live checklist docked in the right sidebar with completed steps struck through, and the inline "Implement this plan?" approval card in the composer](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/100yenadmin/openclaw/c57fe74c64e15e1de7a76e742598904ff207c849/docs/assets/interactive-parity/plan-sidebar.png)

![The exit-plan approval as an inline composer card — Approve or Revise-with-feedback](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/100yenadmin/openclaw/c57fe74c64e15e1de7a76e742598904ff207c849/docs/assets/interactive-parity/plan-approval-inline.png)

### 3 · Goal mode
`/goal set "<objective>" --budget <n>` (or the chip dialog) and walk away. The driver mirrors the Codex goal extension's idle-continuation semantics, adapted honestly to OpenClaw's architecture (no idle event exists — a spike proved the safe shape first): a debounced scheduler armed **only** by turn-completion, firing **only** when four gates pass (goal active · no active run · queue empty · no-progress ceiling not hit), via the cron system-event path + a heartbeat wake. **After a fire it never self-re-arms** — cadence is structurally bounded, no tight loop. Ceiling hit → auto-pause. Budget hit → disarm. The model can only mark `complete|blocked` (host-only pause, mirroring Codex).

![The goal editor modal — objective, token budget, and Save, with the "Pursuing goal" pill live in the composer](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/100yenadmin/openclaw/c57fe74c64e15e1de7a76e742598904ff207c849/docs/assets/interactive-parity/goal-editor.png)

## Security
- **Questions**: human-in-the-loop by construction — no new privilege; answers are typed user input on existing paths; resolution needs the same scopes as approval resolution; proactive push only targets the question's own turn-source chat.
- **Plan gate**: fail-closed at the single choke point, with an **in-PR adversarial suite**: exec, MCP tool, plugin tool, and subagent-spawn are each proven vetoed through the real hook.
- **Goal driver**: a driver-continued turn has exactly the privileges of a user turn — the in-PR safety test raises an exec approval *during* a driver-continued turn and it blocks normally. Layered brakes: debounce+jitter · 4 gates · durable ceiling · budget states · experimental flag (default off).

## Real behavior proof
**Behavior or issue addressed:** agents couldn't ask, couldn't plan reviewably, couldn't pursue; codex `request_user_input` degraded to plain text; `update_plan` events rendered as a bare text line.
**Evidence (full gate on the final tip, run and read by the submitting orchestrator):** 9 backend suites in one run (question manager/wire-contract integration/tool/forwarder/sweep/`/answer` · plan state machine + **adversarial bypass matrix** + approval wire-contract · goal driver loop-safety + integration probe + wiring/safety + commands + durability) — all green; `tsgo` core + test 0; UI suites 781/784 (the 3 = the long-documented `terminal-panel` fixture flake, failing identically on pristine `main` — verified); `ui:i18n:check` clean; `ui:build` 0; **full type-aware `pnpm lint` 0**. The wire-contract integration tests land IN this PR: client↔gateway param drift fails CI here, not in production.

*▶ [Full 30s narrated walkthrough (mp4)](https://github.com/100yenadmin/openclaw/releases/download/interactive-parity-media-v1/parity-demo.mp4) — questions, plan mode, the sidebar plan, inline approval, and goal mode running unattended.*

## Dependency note
No new dependencies; no lockfile change. Plan-mode semantics derive from a 156-case parity-hardened prior implementation; goal-driver semantics mirror `codex-rs/ext/goal` for cross-runtime consistency. Codex plan/goal wire bridges are documented in-code as follow-up seams (hub roadmap) — no speculative plumbing.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw does not currently have an official installable MXC sandbox backend for Windows hosts that can run sandboxed commands through Microsoft eXecution Containers. This leaves MXC-capable Windows environments without a first-party plugin path for ProcessContainer-backed execution and filesystem bridge operations.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds an official OpenShell-style external `mxc` sandbox plugin package (`@openclaw/mxc-sandbox`) with Windows-only readiness checks, plugin-owned MXC SDK dependency ownership, ProcessContainer payload construction, a plugin-side launcher, host-backed filesystem bridge support, sandbox policy loading, and targeted tests.

The plugin source lives under `extensions/mxc`, but it is packaged as an installable plugin (`bundledDist: false`) so the MXC SDK/native dependency is owned by the plugin package instead of an unshipped bundled `node_modules` tree. The backend uses the stable current MXC `0.7.0-alpha` schema and keeps sandbox defaults conservative: curated environments, headless UI, per-exec temp directories, absolute binary overrides, host-derived Windows roots, read-only default workspace access for `none`/`ro`, protected skill overlays for `rw`, and fail-closed unsupported policy handling.

The latest remediation keeps the MXC read-only skill mount resolver plugin-local instead of exporting a new `openclaw/plugin-sdk/sandbox` helper only for this plugin. That preserves the current `>=2026.6.11` host/API floor without claiming a public SDK export that no shipped release tag currently contains.

## User Impact

Users on MXC-capable Windows hosts can install the official MXC sandbox plugin, restart the Gateway, configure `sandbox.backend: "mxc"`, and run OpenClaw sandboxed commands through MXC. Non-Windows or unsupported Windows hosts remain unaffected because the plugin stays dormant when readiness probes fail.

Install command:

```bash
openclaw plugins install @openclaw/mxc-sandbox
```

## Evidence

target.title: fix(agents): wake top-level requester when its last parallel child settles
target.body:
Closes #99395

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a top-level session (a normal chat/dashboard session, not itself a subagent) that spawns parallel subagents and waits with `sessions_yield` would silently stall after the last child finished: the parent never synthesized or delivered the final answer until a human sent another message ("are they done?"). Any fan-out-then-aggregate workflow is affected — e.g. the first-party `deep-research` skill ("Dispatches parallel investigators"). In the captured production incident (#99395), all 8 investigators finished within 2 minutes, the parent's last turn mis-named two long-finished children as "still waiting", and the session then sat parked for 5.5 minutes of total silence until a user ping rescued it. Results whose completion announce gave up (`NO_REPLY` retry exhaustion) were never heard at all.

## Why This Change Was Made

The runtime's "all descendants settled → continue and send your final answer" wake (`wakeSubagentRunAfterDescendants`, from the nested-orchestrator fix #97090) only targets orchestrators that have a subagent-registry run record; a top-level session has none, and the passive per-child announces give it no reliable way to know the batch drained (the injected `## Active Subagents` block vanishes at zero-active, and completion events carry no outstanding count). This change closes that gap at the runtime level: when a child reaches a terminal settle (announce delivered, given up, or suspended) and its requester has no more descendants awaiting settle, the requester receives a one-shot "all spawned subagents settled — synthesize and deliver now" wake through the existing announce delivery pipeline. Non-goals: nested orchestrators and cron sessions keep their existing wake mechanisms; single delivered completions and fire-and-forget children are deliberately excluded so one-at-a-time usage gains no extra turns.

## User Impact

Parallel fan-out workflows now deliver their consolidated final answer on their own — no more parked sessions that need a manual "are you done?" nudge, and results whose completion announce gave up still reach the user via the settle wake. Sequential single-subagent usage, fire-and-forget spawns, nested orchestrators, and cron jobs behave exactly as before.

## Evidence

**Focused unit tests** (new `src/agents/subagent-announce.requester-settle-wake.test.ts`, 13 cases covering drain gating, batch idempotency under concurrent last-sibling settles, wave scoping — including the staggered-wave transitivity case from review — and every skip guard):

```
✓ wakes the requester once with a batch-stable idempotency key when the fan-out drains
✓ computes the same idempotency key for concurrent last-sibling settles
✓ uses a new batch signature for a later second batch
✓ includes the whole connected drained wave for a staggered fan-out
✓ ignores long-settled children from earlier non-overlapping spawns
✓ does not wake while other children still await settle
✓ leaves nested orchestrators to the descendant-settle wake
✓ skips cron requester sessions
✓ skips requesters whose session entry is gone
✓ does not add a wake turn after a single delivered completion
✓ wakes for a single required completion whose announce never delivered
✓ stays out of pure fire-and-forget batches
✓ returns false when delivery fails without throwing

Test Files  1 passed (1)   Tests  13 passed (13)
```

**Full subagent unit + e2e sweep** (all 33 `src/agents/subagent-*` / `openclaw-tools.subagents.*` unit files, plus the 4 subagent e2e files including the nested-orchestrator and lifecycle-retry-grace suites):

```
Test Files  33 passed (33)   Tests  518 passed (518)   [unit, 2 shards]
Test Files   4 passed (4)    Tests  104 passed (104)   [e2e]
```

`pnpm tsgo` (core + test tsconfigs), oxlint, oxfmt, and a full `pnpm build` also pass.

**Give-up path proven in-repo:** `subagent-registry.lifecycle-retry-grace.e2e.test.ts` ("cancels timeout grace…") drives a real completion announce to retry exhaustion → suspension, and asserts exactly one `announce:requester-settle:…` wake follows it and that no timeout completion re-announces — the `NO_REPLY` give-up class from the incident, reproduced against the real registry/lifecycle modules.

**After-fix real-run proof #2 — the production failure class, rescued (2026-07-03, redacted):** a real gateway built from this branch, isolated state dir, real model (`claude-sonnet-4-6` via an OpenAI-compatible proxy), driven by exactly one user message: a deep-research skill task that fanned out **8 investigators in two batches** (5-concurrency staggering, one spawn attempt failed and was retried by the parent), each writing a multi-section report over ~5 minutes. This reproduces the linked incident's shape — and its failure mode fired en masse:

```
14:34:41  user sends the research task                        [the ONLY user message]
14:35:0x  parent spawns 8 investigators (2 batches), yields
14:40–14:53  11 child runs end (incl. parent-driven re-dispatches); EIGHT completion
          announces exhaust retries and give up ("completion agent did not produce a
          visible reply") — the parent NO_REPLYs essentially every completion event.
          On unpatched openclaw this session is now permanently parked.
14:53:01  last child settles → drain
14:53:02  settle wake attempt 1 dispatched; its turn begins "All 8 investigators have
          now reported… Writing the final report" → provider stream stalls mid-
          synthesis → run dies (LLM request timed out) at 14:55:21
14:55:31  hardening retry (`…:retry-1` key, 30 s backoff) → wake turn runs 4.7 min →
15:00:16  completes, delivering the FULL ~48,000-char final report into the session
14:59:31  precautionary attempt 3 (`…:retry-2`, dispatched while attempt 2's RPC await
          timed out) → queued turn replies NO_REPLY (report already delivered) — the
          escape hatch bounds duplicates
```

Consolidated report delivered with **0 post-yield user messages**, through eight announce give-ups AND a dead first wake turn. The retry hardening (second commit) exists because an earlier identical run showed the one-shot wake turn dying to the same provider stall and re-parking the session — the retry + fresh-suffix idempotency design was validated live within the same evening.

**After-fix real-run proof #1 — clean mechanics (2026-07-03, redacted):** same setup, one user message: *"Spawn exactly THREE subagents in parallel via sessions_spawn … sessions_yield … send one consolidated summary titled ANIMAL FACTS ROUNDUP."* No further input was sent. Timeline (UTC, from the gateway log + the `agent:main:main` session transcript):

```
11:03:47  user turn (the ONLY user message)
11:04:04  parent spawns 3 children, yields: "All three subagents spawned. Waiting for all to complete."
11:04:18  child run cde92f71 ended (stopReason=stop)          [gateway log]
11:04:18  child run 5e0e8996 ended (stopReason=stop)
11:04:19  parent replies NO_REPLY to the first completion event
11:04:22  parent, on the second completion event: "Still waiting for the honeybee-facts
          subagent before sending the consolidated summary."   [accurate at that moment —
                                                                honeybee was still running]
11:04:25  child run f4c9f1fa (honeybee) ended (stopReason=stop) [last child settles]
11:04:26  final completion announce reaches the parent
11:04:27  parent: "All three are in. Here's the consolidated summary: # ANIMAL FACTS ROUNDUP …"
11:04:45  run announce:requester-settle:agent:main:main:5e0e8996…,cde92f71…,f4c9f1fa… ended
          [the new settle wake — batch-stable idempotency key covering all 3 children, carrying
           "[Subagent Context] Every subagent spawned from this session has now settled … send your
           consolidated final answer to the user now" + all three children's findings]
11:04:45  parent replies NO_REPLY to the wake                   [answer already delivered — the
                                                                escape hatch suppressing a duplicate]
```

Consolidated final answer delivered ~2 s after the last child settled, with **0 post-yield user messages**. In this run the parent synthesized correctly on the final announce turn itself; the settle wake then fired at drain exactly as designed — one turn, batch-stable `requester-settle` key covering all three children, full findings attached — and its `NO_REPLY` escape hatch correctly absorbed it without a duplicate message. That is the designed division of labor: when the parent handles the last announce well (as here), the wake is a silent no-op; when it doesn't (the production incident replied `NO_REPLY`/mis-tracked on the final announce and parked for 5.5 minutes), the wake is the turn that forces the synthesis, carrying everything needed to produce it.

**Live observation (production, openclaw 2026.6.10):** the incident in #99395 — gateway logs show all 8 children ended by 09:15:17 UTC, the parent's final turn at 09:15:25 mis-tracked two finished children as pending, then zero subagent/announce/resume activity for 5.5 minutes until the user's 09:20:45 ping. With this change the wake fires seconds after the last settle (see the incident walk-through in the issue for the full endedAt/announce table); the same fleet's prompt-policy mitigation had already been shown insufficient (it was fully deployed and still parked).

**Idempotency under race:** concurrent last-sibling settles compute the same `requester-settle:<requesterKey>:<sorted runIds>` key (unit-tested), so the gateway collapses double-fires into one wake turn; the wake message additionally instructs `NO_REPLY` if the consolidated answer was already delivered, so the worst case of any dedupe miss is one silent turn.

**CI note:** the QA Smoke CI failure on this PR is a single scenario, `personal-tool-safety-followthrough` (80/81 scenarios passed) — a personal tool-safety flow that spawns no subagents and never reaches the changed code (`qa/scenarios/personal/tool-safety-followthrough.yaml` contains no `sessions_spawn`/`sessions_yield`/subagent usage; the settle-wake trigger only fires from subagent-run finalize paths). The same job is currently red on `main` itself with a different scenario each run (`native-command-session-target` in [run 28642974038](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28642974038) and [run 28641562098](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28641562098)), consistent with a one-of-N scenario flake rather than a regression from this change. Happy to have the job re-run.

## Implementation notes

- **`hasDescendantRunAwaitingSettle`** (`src/agents/subagent-registry-queries.ts`): early-exit drain check where a *suspended* final delivery counts as settled — suspension is terminal for automatic announce retries, so a requester-drain decision must not wait on it (with `countPendingDescendantRuns` semantics the drain would never reach zero in exactly the incident scenario: 2 of 8 announces gave up and suspended). Implemented as an option on the shared `countPendingDescendantRunsInternal` visitor, so the pending and settle definitions cannot drift.
- **`maybeWakeRequesterAfterAllChildrenSettled`** (`src/agents/subagent-announce.ts`): scopes the wake batch to the settling child's **parallel wave — the connected component of lifetime overlaps** seeded at the settling run. Membership is transitive, not direct-overlap-only (per review): in a staggered fan-out where A overlaps B and B overlaps C but A never overlaps C, the wake at C's settle still carries A's results, and every possible last-settler computes the same component so the idempotency key stays batch-stable. Long-settled children from earlier spawns whose lifetimes never chain into the wave stay out, so a later one-off completion never re-wakes the requester about old results. Fires only for ≥ 2 required completions in the wave or ≥ 1 undelivered required completion; skips nested (depth ≥ 1) and cron requesters; defers session-store reads until the in-memory registry gating passes (this runs on every child settle fleet-wide); reuses `buildChildCompletionFindings` so the wake carries the wave's results; delivers via `deliverSubagentAnnouncement` (active requesters get it steered into the live turn, parked ones get a new origin-routed turn).

Fire-and-forget — settle bookkeeping never blocks on the wake.
- **Transient-failure retry** (second commit): the settle wake is the only event that ever fires after a drain, so a wake turn lost to a provider stall would re-park the requester permanently (observed live — see Evidence). Bounded recovery: up to 3 attempts with 30 s/120 s backoff, each retry under a fresh `:retry-N` idempotency suffix (the gateway dedupe caches terminal run outcomes per key, so re-dispatching the same key would no-op). A legitimately silent wake reply already classifies as delivered and never retries; terminal failures and an abandoned requester stop immediately.

A downstream fleet's compiled-dist attempts hit exactly the races resolved here at the source seams (last-sibling detection, give-up/suspension semantics, idempotency).
- **Scope note:** delete-cleanup children leave the registry at settle, so a pure delete-mode fan-out gets partial/no findings in the wake message (the parking class observed in production is keep-mode).

target.title: fix(slack): suppress progress chrome sends
target.body:
## Summary
- detect progress-only Slack tool chrome payloads with leading tool emoji plus command/status body
- convert thread-scoped chrome to reactions instead of chat.postMessage
- fail closed by suppressing chrome without a reaction target while preserving semantic replies

## What Problem This Solves
Progress-only operational chrome like `:hammer_and_wrench: `pnpm test`` or `:writing_hand: Write: MEMORY.md` can leak into Slack as user-visible messages when a tool/status payload accidentally reaches the Slack send path. This creates noise in working channels and violates the progress-chrome pre-send gate. The Slack extension now classifies only narrow progress-only payloads and prevents them from becoming chat posts.

## Evidence
- `CI=true pnpm oxfmt --check extensions/slack/src/send.ts extensions/slack/src/send.identity-fallback.test.ts extensions/slack/src/blocks.test-helpers.ts`
- `CI=true pnpm vitest run extensions/slack/src/send.identity-fallback.test.ts` (15 tests)
- `CI=true pnpm tsgo:extensions`
- `git diff --check`

## Verification
- Thread-scoped progress chrome converts to `reactions.add` instead of `chat.postMessage`.
- Progress chrome without a reaction target is suppressed before Slack post.
- Semantic replies using the same leading emoji remain sendable.

## Summary

Fixes static provider catalog conversion so resolved runtime models preserve schema-valid provider/model metadata.

## Problem

Static catalog providers can define provider-level request `params`, while individual model rows can define model-level `params`, `compat`, and `mediaInput`. The static catalog conversion path was not preserving that metadata consistently, so downstream model resolution and OpenAI-compatible payload construction could lose information that other configured-provider paths already keep.

The concrete gap fixed here is provider/model metadata propagation in `modelFromProviderStaticCatalog`.

## Changes

- Merge provider-level and model-level `params` when building a runtime model from the static catalog.
- Let model-level `params` override provider-level defaults.
- Preserve model `compat` metadata on the resolved runtime model.
- Preserve model `mediaInput` metadata on the resolved runtime model.
- Add regression coverage for static catalog metadata preservation, tool-capability checks, and OpenAI-compatible payload construction.

## Real behavior proof

target.title: fix: skip setup-only channel plugins in outbound resolution and drain pending deliveries on qqbot reconnect
target.body:
## Summary

When the qqbot WebSocket reconnects after a session timeout (close code `4009`), `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()` returns a setup-only plugin stub that lacks any send capability. This causes the `"Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"` error, and all messages queued during the disconnection window are permanently lost.

## Root Cause

`resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()` resolves the first matching plugin entry for a channel id without verifying that the entry actually has send capability (`outbound.sendText`, `message.send.text`, etc.). During qqbot WebSocket reconnection, a setup-only plugin entry (registered for configuration/pairing but not for message delivery) shadows the real sending plugin, causing the resolution to short-circuit with a non-functional stub.

Regression introduced in 2026.5.28 (commit `e932160`).

## Fix

### 1. Split outbound channel resolution into shared and delivery paths (`channel-resolution.ts`)

Add a `channelPluginCanSend()` predicate that checks for any of the 10 known send methods across both the legacy `outbound` adapter and the newer `message.send` adapter:

- `outbound.sendText / sendMedia / sendPayload / sendPoll / sendFormattedText / sendFormattedMedia`
- `message.send.text / media / payload / poll`

Instead of gating the shared `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()` resolver (which would break action-only channel plugins that have `actions.handleAction` but no send capability), a new **`resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery()`** resolver applies the send-capability guard exclusively for message delivery paths.

- **`resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()`**: Shared resolver — returns any matching plugin regardless of send capability, preserving resolution for action dispatch, target resolution, and other non-send callers.
- **`resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery()`**: Delivery resolver — skips setup-only entries and only returns plugins that can actually send messages.
- **`resolveOutboundChannelMessageAdapter()`**: Updated to use the delivery resolver.
- **`message.ts`**: `sendMessage`/`sendPoll` updated to use the delivery resolver.

### 2. Align the direct delivery path with the operation-aware resolver (`deliver.ts`)

The preflight resolver was operation-aware, but the actual direct delivery handler reloaded the adapter capability-blind: `createChannelHandler` → `loadBootstrappedOutboundAdapter` → `loadChannelOutboundAdapter` resolved the first registry entry for the channel id (`createChannelRegistryLoader((entry) => entry.plugin.outbound)`) without checking send capability. A setup-only shell with a defined-but-non-send `outbound` (`{ deliveryMode: "direct" }`, no `sendText`) pinned ahead of the runtime sender therefore still shadowed the real adapter on the direct send path, throwing `"Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"` even after preflight had selected a valid plugin. This also affected the reconnect drain path, which has no preflight.

`loadBootstrappedOutboundAdapter` now resolves through the same `resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery()` resolver as preflight (with `allowBootstrap`, operation `text`), so preflight and the actual direct delivery handler share one send-capability-aware resolution path. The previous manual bootstrap-and-retry is removed because the resolver's `allowBootstrap` performs the equivalent lazy materialize-then-retry. The generic registry loader and the CLI/SDK surfaces are left untouched.

### 3. Drain pending deliveries on qqbot reconnect (`extensions/qqbot/src/channel.ts`)

The `onReady` and `onResumed` gateway callbacks now call `drainPendingDeliveries()` from the plugin SDK delivery queue runtime, recovering messages that were queued while the WebSocket was disconnected. The drain is:

- Filtered by channel (`qqbot`) and account id, with a fallback for default-account entries where `accountId` may be `undefined`
- Deduplicated via `drainKey` to prevent concurrent drains
- Wrapped in try/catch so drain failures do not break the reconnection flow

### 4. Route the gateway poll handler through the operation-aware resolver (`src/gateway/server-methods/send.ts`)

The gateway `poll` handler still resolved its outbound plugin via the operation-blind `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()`, while `sendPoll` (`message.ts`) and the direct text delivery path (`deliver.ts`) already routed through the operation-aware `resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery()`. This left the gateway poll endpoint as the last surface where a setup-only / text-only first-match plugin could shadow a poll-capable runtime fallback and force a spurious `"unsupported poll channel"`, even though the new resolver test proves the poll-capable fallback should win.

The poll handler now resolves through `resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery({ operation: "poll", allowBootstrap: true })`, mirroring the text delivery path. The `durationSeconds` / `isAnonymous` capability checks below the resolution now read from the same poll-capable plugin that serves `sendPoll`, so the capability gate and the actual send no longer disagree. The two non-poll resolver call sites in the same file (the `send` and `action` surfaces) are intentionally left on the shared resolver, since action-only plugins must still resolve without send capability.

## Tests

- `channel-resolution.test.ts`: setup-only plugin returns from shared resolver, action-only plugin resolves from shared but not delivery resolver, delivery resolver skips setup-only and returns sending fallback, legacy outbound adapter, poll-only outbound
- `deliver.test.ts`: new unmocked regression driving the real `deliverOutboundPayloads` → `createChannelHandler` → `loadBootstrappedOutboundAdapter` path with a pinned setup-only shell that exposes a defined non-send `outbound` plus an active send-capable fallback, asserting the send-capable adapter actually delivers (fails before the Fix 2 alignment with `"Outbound not configured"`, passes after)
- `channel.test.ts`: onReady drain, onResumed drain

Fixes #88955.


## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: After a QQ Bot WebSocket disconnect (session takeover / close code 4009), `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()` returned a setup-only plugin stub instead of the runtime entry, causing `"Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"` and dropping all pending deliveries.

- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw `2026.6.2` (commit `b90683e`, branch `fix/qqbot-reconnect-outbound-88955`), macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0. QQ Bot plugin `@openclaw/qqbot@2026.5.31-beta.4` with live QQ Bot credentials (appId `<redacted>`).

- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  1. Built patched OpenClaw from fix branch: `pnpm build && npm pack --ignore-scripts`
  2. Installed globally: `npm install -g openclaw-2026.6.2.tgz` — confirmed version: `OpenClaw 2026.6.2 (b90683e)`
  3. Restarted gateway: `openclaw gateway restart`
  4. Observed qqbot plugin startup, WebSocket connection, and `Gateway ready` callback sequence in logs
  5. Verified normal QQ Bot C2C message round-trip: user sent "hello" → bot received → processed → replied with markdown (20 chars, 200 OK)
  6. Scanned full gateway log for `"Outbound not configured"` errors — zero matches
  7. Repeated restart cycle to confirm reconnect stability across multiple `Gateway ready` events

- **Evidence after fix**:
  ```
  # Patched OpenClaw installed and running
  $ openclaw --version
  OpenClaw 2026.6.2 (b90683e)

  # Gateway restart sequence — qqbot reconnects cleanly
  2026-06-02T22:38:53.727+08:00 [gateway] received SIGTERM; restarting
  2026-06-02T22:39:15.986+08:00 [gateway] http server listening (8 plugins: ..., qqbot, ...; 1.6s)
  2026-06-02T22:39:16.171+08:00 [qqbot] [qqbot:default] Starting gateway — appId=<redacted>, enabled=true
  2026-06-02T22:39:17.387+08:00 [qqbot] [default] Connecting to wss://api.sgroup.qq.com/websocket
  2026-06-02T22:39:18.468+08:00 [qqbot] [default] WebSocket connected
  2026-06-02T22:39:18.641+08:00 [qqbot] [qqbot:default] Gateway ready

  # Successful QQ Bot message delivery after reconnect
  2026-06-02T22:32:40.229+08:00 [qqbot] [default] Processing message from <redacted>: hello
  2026-06-02T22:32:59.431+08:00 [qqbot] [default] [qqbot:api] <<< Status: 200 OK
  2026-06-02T22:32:59.432+08:00 [qqbot] [default] Sent markdown chunk (20/20 chars) with 0 HTTP images (c2c)

  # Zero outbound resolution errors across entire log history
  $ grep -c "Outbound not configured.*qqbot" ~/Library/Logs/openclaw/gateway.log
  0

  # Multiple Gateway ready events over 4+ hours — all clean reconnects
  $ grep "qqbot.*Gateway ready" ~/Library/Logs/openclaw/gateway.log | wc -l
  18
  ```

- **Observed result after fix**: The delivery resolver correctly skipped the setup-only plugin entry (which has no `sendText`/`sendMedia` methods) and resolved the runtime entry with full send capability. Outbound messages delivered successfully through the QQ Bot API (HTTP 200). Zero occurrences of the `"Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"` error across 18 reconnect cycles over a 4+ hour observation window. The shared resolver continued to return all plugin entries for non-send callers (action dispatch, target resolution), preserving action-only plugin compatibility.

- **Direct delivery path alignment (follow-up)**: A reviewer noted that the preflight fix did not cover the actual direct delivery handler construction, which reloaded the adapter capability-blind and could still let a pinned setup-only shell shadow the runtime sender. `loadBootstrappedOutboundAdapter` now routes through the same `resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery()` resolver as preflight. Verified locally on the fix branch (macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0): the new unmocked `deliver.test.ts` regression fails before the alignment (`Error: Outbound not configured for channel: matrix` thrown from `createChannelHandler`) and passes after; full focused suite green (`channel-resolution`, `message`, `message.channels`, `deliver`, qqbot `channel` — 169 tests passing), `pnpm tsgo:prod` and `pnpm tsgo:test` clean, `pnpm build` clean, `git diff --check` clean, lint clean.

- **Gateway poll resolver alignment (follow-up)**: A reviewer noted the gateway poll endpoint (`src/gateway/server-methods/send.ts`) still used the operation-blind `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()`, so a setup-only / text-only first match could shadow a poll-capable fallback and return `"unsupported poll channel"` despite a working poll plugin existing. The poll handler now routes through `resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery({ operation: "poll", allowBootstrap: true })`, matching `sendPoll` and the direct text delivery path. Verified locally on the fix branch (macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0): a new gateway `send.test.ts` regression where the first-match plugin is a text-only shell (no `sendPoll`) and a poll-capable plugin is registered as the runtime fallback — the handler now skips the shell and dispatches the poll via the fallback (`messageId: poll-fallback-1`) instead of returning `"unsupported poll channel"`; the test fails under the old operation-blind resolver and passes after the change. Full gateway send suite green (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/send.test.ts` — 124 tests passing), `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:test:src` clean. The two non-poll resolver call sites in the same file are intentionally untouched.

- **What was not tested**:

  Live drain proof is not reproducible on the fixed build. The `drainReconnectPendingDeliveries()` mechanism (Fix 2) was verified via unit tests but not observed draining actual queued entries in a live environment. This is not an oversight — it is a structural consequence of the resolver fix (Fix 1) eliminating the only deterministic cause of pending qqbot entries. Code-level analysis confirms this:

  **How the delivery queue works** (`deliver.ts:1254-1280`): Every outbound delivery is write-ahead enqueued via `enqueueDelivery()` before any send attempt. On success, `ackDelivery()` removes the entry (`deliver.ts:1367`). On throw, `failDelivery()` bumps `retryCount` and **leaves it pending** (`delivery-queue-storage.ts:137-144`).

  **What created the pending entries in #88955**: The `"Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"` throw fired from `createChannelHandler` (`deliver.ts:223-231`) when `resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery` returned a setup-only plugin with no send methods. This throw occurs **outside** the per-payload try/catch (`deliver.ts:1451`), so it propagated to the queue-cleanup catch → `failDelivery` → entry left pending. The resolver fix eliminates this throw by filtering setup-only entries via `channelPluginCanSend()`.

  **Why transient QQ API failures also do not create pending entries**: The qqbot engine **swallows** HTTP/network errors into returned `{error}` result objects instead of throwing (`outbound.ts:301-304, 313-318`). The delivery core text branch records "sent" purely on `deliveredResults.length > 0` with no message-id identity gate (`deliver.ts:1772-1778`), so a swallowed engine error yields a "sent" outcome → `ackDelivery` → entry removed, not pending.

  **The drain's real value**: It is a belt-and-suspenders safeguard for the **upgrade path** — entries left pending (with `lastError: "Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"`) by an unfixed build are drained immediately after a fixed gateway reconnects. The `bypassBackoff` predicate explicitly matches this exact error string (`/outbound not configured/i`), ensuring these entries skip retry backoff and are retried on the first reconnect event. If the retry still fails (e.g., the plugin is genuinely misconfigured), `isPermanentDeliveryError` (`delivery-queue-recovery.ts:79`) moves the entry to `failed/` — no infinite retry loop. `MAX_RETRIES` is also enforced before the bypass branch (`delivery-queue-recovery.ts:544`). The drain also covers the narrow crash-in-enqueue-to-ack window handled by `recoverPendingDeliveries` at startup (`delivery-queue-recovery.ts:604`). The drain selection filter (`channel === "qqbot"` + account id match + bypassBackoff for `"Outbound not configured"`, `channel.test.ts:90-152`) and the reconnect-drain integration logic (`delivery-queue.reconnect-drain.test.ts`) are exercised by 35 unit tests (all passing).

  **Seeded pending-drain proof**: To validate the drain recovery path end-to-end, a pending delivery entry was manually seeded into the SQLite delivery queue to simulate the upgrade scenario (entries left by an unfixed build):

  1. Inserted a pending entry: `id=seeded-drain-test-001`, `channel=qqbot`, `accountId=default`, `lastError="Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"`, `retry_count=1`
  2. Restarted gateway: `openclaw gateway restart`
  3. Observed recovery sequence in logs:

  ```
  00:30:00.353 [gateway] http server listening (8 plugins: ..., qqbot, ...; 1.9s)
  00:30:00.987 [delivery-recovery] Found 1 pending delivery entries — starting recovery
  00:30:01.567 [qqbot] [qqbot:api] <<< Status: 200 OK
  00:30:02.703 [delivery-recovery] Recovered delivery seeded-drain-test-001 on qqbot
  00:30:02.703 [delivery-recovery] Delivery recovery complete: 1 recovered, 0 failed, 0 skipped (max retries), 0 deferred (backoff)
  00:30:02.816 [qqbot] [default] WebSocket connected
  00:30:02.952 [qqbot] [qqbot:default] Gateway ready
  ```

  4. Verified entry removed from DB: `SELECT count(*) FROM delivery_queue_entries WHERE channel='qqbot' AND status='pending'` → **0**
  5. Zero `"Outbound not configured"` errors after restart

target.title: /learn's skill-authoring-and-apply pipeline has no owner gate, unlike the equivalent plugin-install path
target.body:
## Summary

`/learn` and its underlying `skill_workshop` agent tool and `/approve` submission path have no owner check anywhere in the chain, unlike the equivalent plugin-install path. Any sender in `commands.allowFrom` (not necessarily the configured owner) can author a new skill, apply it into the shared workspace `skills/` directory, and self-approve the required approval gate in the same chat, on the default (unconfigured) approvers posture that essentially every built-in channel ships with.

## Environment

- Commit: 9f248969f6c81141f8a513cb8b9209fe09d29b33 (origin/main at time of filing)
- Surface: `/learn` command handler, `skill_workshop` agent tool, `/approve` command handler; channel-agnostic (reproduced against the internal/webchat-style command path with no channel plugin configured)

## Steps to reproduce

1. A sender who is in `commands.allowFrom` but is not the owner (`senderIsOwner: false`) sends `/learn write a skill that does X`. `commands-learn.ts:184` gates this with `rejectUnauthorizedCommand`, which only checks `isAuthorizedSender` (`command-gates.ts:16-30`), not `rejectNonOwnerCommand`/`senderIsOwner` (`command-gates.ts:32-46`).
2. The agent calls the `skill_workshop` tool with `action="create"` and drafts a proposal, then calls it again with `action="apply"`. `skill-workshop-tool.ts`'s `execute()` (lines ~143-277) performs no sender-identity check for any of its 8 actions; `action="apply"` (~170-181) calls `applySkillProposal` in `service.ts` (538-624) directly.
3. `applySkillProposal` writes the proposal markdown straight into `<workspaceDir>/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` and calls `bumpSkillsSnapshotVersion` (607-611), so the new skill is immediately auto-discovered by every future conversation with that agent, including the owner's own.
4. The only brake is `resolveSkillWorkshopToolApproval` in `policy.ts` (144-176), which by default (`approvalPolicy: "pending"`) requires a `plugin.approval.resolve` decision. The same non-owner sender submits that decision via `/approve <id> allow` in the same chat. `commands-approve.ts:177` gates this with `!params.command.isAuthorizedSender && !hasExplicitApprovalAuthorization` - again `isAuthorizedSender`, not `senderIsOwner`.
5. The authorization behind that decision, `resolveApprovalCommandAuthorization` in `channel-approval-auth.ts`, does not take `senderIsOwner` as an input at all. When the channel has no separately configured `approvers`/`ownerAllowFrom` (the default for essentially every built-in channel), the underlying adapter (`approval-auth-helpers.ts:85-89`, `createResolvedApproverActionAuthAdapter`) returns `markImplicitSameChatApprovalAuthorization({ authorized: true })` unconditionally - anyone in the chat, regardless of owner status. For non-channel-plugin surfaces, `channel-approval-auth.ts` returns `{ authorized: true, explicit: false }` directly, again with no owner check.

Compare to `/plugins install|enable|disable`, which is hard owner-gated via `rejectNonOwnerCommand` at `commands-plugins.ts:465-472` for the same class of workspace-write operation.

## Expected

Authoring and applying a new skill (or approving that application) should require the same owner-tier check as installing a plugin: `rejectNonOwnerCommand`/`senderIsOwner`, not merely `isAuthorizedSender`.

## Actual

A non-owner authorized sender can single-handedly draft, apply, and self-approve a brand-new skill with zero owner participation, landing it in the shared workspace `skills/` directory at the same trust tier as an owner-approved skill.

## Root cause

- `src/auto-reply/reply/commands-learn.ts:184-190` - entry gate uses `rejectUnauthorizedCommand`, not `rejectNonOwnerCommand`.
- `src/agents/tools/skill-workshop-tool.ts:36-45,143-277` - `execute()` performs no identity check for any action, including `apply`.
- `src/skills/workshop/service.ts:538-624` - `applySkillProposal` writes directly into `workspaceDir/skills` and bumps the snapshot version with no owner check in the chain.
- `src/skills/workshop/policy.ts:9,144-176` - the approval gate only checks `config.approvalPolicy`, not sender identity.
- `src/auto-reply/reply/commands-approve.ts:177` - approval submission gate checks `isAuthorizedSender`, not `senderIsOwner`.
- `src/plugin-sdk/approval-auth-helpers.ts:85-89` - implicit same-chat fallback grants `authorized: true` unconditional on owner status when no approvers are configured.
- `src/auto-reply/reply/commands-plugins.ts:465-472` - sibling `/plugins` write path, for comparison, does call `rejectNonOwnerCommand`.

## Sibling surfaces

`/plugins install|enable|disable` is unaffected; it already owner-gates via `rejectNonOwnerCommand`. Did not check every other command tied to `plugin.approval.resolve`/`exec.approval.resolve` beyond `/learn` and `skill_workshop`; other tools that route lifecycle mutations through the same `resolveApprovalCommandAuthorization` implicit-fallback path may share this gap and were not individually enumerated here.

## Real behavior proof
Behavior addressed: non-owner authorized sender can author, apply, and self-approve a new skill through /learn with no owner check anywhere in the chain
Real environment tested: real production functions driven directly at commit 9f248969f6c81141f8a513cb8b9209fe09d29b33 - handleLearnCommand from src/auto-reply/reply/commands-learn.ts, createSkillWorkshopTool().execute from src/agents/tools/skill-workshop-tool.ts (real filesystem writes under a temp workspaceDir, real applySkillProposal from src/skills/workshop/service.ts), and resolveApprovalCommandAuthorization from src/infra/channel-approval-auth.ts
Exact steps or command run after this patch: drove handleLearnCommand(params, true) with command.isAuthorizedSender=true and command.senderIsOwner=false; drove createSkillWorkshopTool({ workspaceDir, config: {} }).execute with action="create" then action="apply" and no sender-identity argument of any kind; drove resolveApprovalCommandAuthorization({ cfg, channel, senderId: "not-the-owner", kind: "plugin" }) with no channels.*.execApprovals/approvers configured
Evidence after fix:
```
learn_gate_nonowner_shouldContinue=true senderIsOwner=false isAuthorizedSender=true
learn_gate_unauthorized_shouldContinue=false senderIsOwner=false isAuthorizedSender=false
skill_workshop_apply_status=applied sender_identity_param_passed_to_execute=none
skill_file_written=/tmp/owner-gate-repro-LHC4uM/dir-0/skills/exfil-helper/SKILL.md
skill_file_content=---
name: "exfil-helper"
description: "Demonstrates unattended skill authoring"
---

# Exfil Helper

Do the thing an owner never reviewed.
approve_authorization_nonowner={"authorized":true,"explicit":false} function_signature_has_senderIsOwner_param=false
```
Observed result after fix: the /learn gate lets a non-owner authorized sender through (shouldContinue=true) while correctly still blocking a fully unauthorized sender in the control run; the skill_workshop tool applies a proposal straight to a live SKILL.md file on disk with no sender-identity parameter available anywhere in its execute signature to check; and resolveApprovalCommandAuthorization grants authorized=true for a non-owner sender because its own parameter list has no senderIsOwner field to consult, confirming the gap spans the entry gate, the tool, and the approval-submission path
What was not tested: did not exercise a real end-to-end chat transcript through a live channel plugin (Telegram/Discord/WhatsApp) with an actual configured approver list set to a different user than the sender; did not check every other tool wired through the same plugin.approval.resolve implicit-fallback path beyond skill_workshop for the identical gap

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

- Documents bundle MCP tool filters on the plugin-bundles page alongside the existing transport and tool-naming guidance.

target.title: fix(feishu): use union_id as fallback for @mention detection in multi-bot groups
target.body:
## Problem

Fixes #40768

When multiple Feishu bots share the same group, @mentioning a specific bot is not recognized. The bot logs `message in group ... did not mention bot` even though it's correctly mentioned.

## Root Cause

Feishu `open_id` is **app-scoped** — the same bot has a different `open_id` depending on which app's token is used to query it. Confirmed by querying the same message with two different bot tokens:

```
# Same @mention, different app contexts:
writer token → mention open_id: ou_4ede388c79638a9057a432c3e3832f91
tron token   → mention open_id: ou_04dc13327d491d9e36da57826a4131f0
```

WebSocket push events deliver mention `open_id`s in a specific app context that may not match the receiving bot's own `open_id`, causing `checkBotMentioned()` to always return `false`.

## Fix

`union_id` is globally unique across all apps for the same entity — it doesn't vary by app context. This PR:

1. Fetches `union_id` alongside `open_id` from `bot/v3/info` at startup
2. Stores it in a new `botUnionIds` map in monitor state
3. Passes it through to `checkBotMentioned()` as a fallback
4. Matches mentions by `union_id` when `open_id` doesn't match

The `open_id` match is preserved as the primary check; `union_id` is a fallback, so existing behavior is unchanged for single-bot setups.

## Files Changed

- `types.ts`: add `botUnionId` to `FeishuProbeResult`
- `probe.ts`: extract `union_id` from `bot/v3/info` response
- `monitor.startup.ts`: propagate `botUnionId` through `FeishuMonitorBotIdentity`
- `monitor.state.ts`: add `botUnionIds` map with proper clear/delete
- `monitor.account.ts`: store/clear `botUnionId`, pass to `handleFeishuMessage`
- `bot.ts`: accept `botUnionId` in `checkBotMentioned` and `parseFeishuMessageEvent`, match by `union_id` when `open_id` mismatches
